alerts.title: Anthropic-Pentagon: 7% to 14%, rising

what_moved.event: Financial Times and Bloomberg report Amodei resumed negotiations with Emil Michael. New prototype agreement with $200M ceiling awarded.
Anthropic files second lawsuit against the Department of Defense.
Judge moves hearing from April 3 to March 24. TIME publishes profile of Anthropic.
Anthropic lawyers tell the court the designation could cost billions. Revenue hits $19B annualized, up from $14B weeks earlier.

nodes.name: Emil Michael
nodes.role: Undersecretary of Defense for R&E. Directly negotiating with Amodei.

nodes.name: Pete Hegseth
nodes.role: Secretary of Defense. Set the Friday 5PM deadline. Declared Anthropic a supply chain risk.

nodes.name: David Sacks
nodes.role: White House AI Czar. Invested in xAI via Craft Ventures. xAI benefits if Anthropic excluded.

nodes.name: OpenAI
nodes.role: Secured $200M Pentagon deal hours after Anthropic collapse. Direct competitor and beneficiary.

nodes.name: Palantir
nodes.role: Classified AI infra for Pentagon. Now monitors Polymarket (sports, as of Mar 10). Employee first raised Claude use in Venezuela raid.

alerts.assessment: The market is pricing the reopened negotiations. The hearing acceleration to March 24 compresses the timeline. An independent forecaster (Nathan P.M. Young, Substack, March 12) estimates 7% via Monte Carlo, diverging from Polymarket's 14%. The next data point is March 24: the court hearing.
